items.title: Chico Freeman interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 13, 2001
items.q: I was playing on this classical mouthpiece, you know, a Selmer C Star.

ctx.x: Well it was kind of funny because I can tell you, he didn’t hear it. But it was kind of interesting, he was conducting these jam sessions in Chicago. And I mean everybody that came through town came there afterwards, from Rahsaan Roland Kirk, Clifford Jordan, Sonny Rollins, you name it. They would work the places in Chicago and afterwards they’d go to wherever my Dad—And I used to go down there on the weekends and just listen and I got exposed to like all the players from out of the city, from New York and other…

You know it. Right. And I was in the saxophone quartet in school. But you know I got up there on the bandstand, and if I remember correctly, it was my father and maybe Clifford Jordan might have been there and a couple of other people. And all these big saxophones — and here Chicago is known for big sounds you know. And my sound sounded like I was tearing paper. And I became totally, almost it was disheartening. Because there was just no sound. I mean it was great sound for the classical thing but it was terrible…
